question.question: A company has an equity value of £1,000m, debt of £400m and cash of £100m. What is its enterprise value, and why do you subtract the cash?
question.model_answer_md: Enterprise value is £1,300m: equity value £1,000m plus net debt of £300m (debt £400m less cash £100m). Cash is subtracted because an acquirer effectively gets it back on day one — it can be used to repay debt — so it is not part of the price of the operating business.
key_points: Cash is subtracted because the acquirer gets it back / it can pay down debt
question.weak_answer_note: Adding cash instead of subtracting it, or subtracting it twice; forgetting to state the number.

answer: So EV is equity value plus net debt, um, net debt is debt minus cash so 400 minus 100 is 300, so EV is 1,300 million. You take cash off because when you buy the company you get the cash, it's not really part of the operating business.
